title: Gaia DR3 velocities exclude on-target eclipsing binaries for TESS candidates TIC 67502817.01 (4.11 h) and TIC 63562537.01 (5.51 h); TRICERATOPS rates both likely planets without imaging
abstract: Question: Are the two ultra-short-period TESS candidates from a prior campaign search of M dwarfs (sci:sha256:5df2cf96) planets or false positives? TIC 67502817.01 (P = 4.108 h, 597 ppm, 1.67 Earth radii) would have the shortest period of the known transiting planets around main-sequence stars. TIC 63562537.01 has P = 5.51 h and 1.0 Earth radius. Approach: No new TESS sectors exist. We re-analysed the same sectors with an independent pipeline (QLP), used Gaia DR3 RVS epoch-velocity scatter and one LAMOST velocity per star, simulated the Gaia DR3 RUWE response to bound companions with the real Gaia scan times, ran TRICERATOPS (two seeds; local TRILEGAL file; one-line fix for the current TESScut format), and scanned the period aliases. Results: Both transits are present in every sector and in QLP. Gaia velocities limit the semi-amplitude to below 9.6 km/s and 1.4 km/s (99 %), against 30-39 km/s for a 0.08 solar-mass companion. Thus eclipsing binaries on the target are excluded, and for TIC 63562537 also companions above 2.9 Jupiter masses. Without imaging, TRICERATOPS gives FPP = 0.16 and 0.11 (NFPP 9e-4 and 4e-4) for TIC 67502817.01 and FPP = 0.044 and 0.025 (NFPP 2e-8) for TIC 63562537.01: likely planets, not validated. All EB scenarios are below 1e-5. The FPP comes from a planet on an unresolved bound companion. Gaia RUWE excludes most companions brighter than 4 mag only inside 0.1 arcsec (TIC 67502817) and 0.2-0.3 arcsec (TIC 63562537). With a hypothetical speckle non-detection, FPP would fall to 4e-4 for TIC 63562537.01 but only to 0.036 (NFPP 1.1e-3) for TIC 67502817.01. For TIC 63562537.01 the 0.2297013 d alias is preferred over 0.2297739 d by delta chi-square 1.6-5.0, which is not decisive. The occultation of TIC 67502817.01 is -2 +/- 60 ppm, which agrees with a dark rocky planet but does not discriminate. Limitations: same TESS photons as the discovery; approximate mass-magnitude relation and noise model in the RUWE simulation; TRICERATOPS Monte Carlo scatter of about 30 %; hypothetical contrast curve. Neither candidate is confirmed or validated. Imaging, precise radial velocities and ground photometry of the 15-arcsec neighbour of TIC 67502817 are the next steps. display.caption: Phase-folded TESS photometry of both candidates. Top: SPOC 2-minute and TESS-SPOC FFI light curves with the joint transit fit. Bottom: the same data from the independent QLP pipeline. The shaded band is the occultation window at phase 0.5.

Summary of the false-positive constraints. Left: TRICERATOPS scenario probabilities (two seeds, no imaging). Right: Gaia DR3 RVS limit on the velocity semi-amplitude of an on-target companion, compared with the amplitude of a 0.08 solar-mass companion.

Fraction of simulated bound stellar companions that would raise the Gaia DR3 RUWE above 1.4, against projected separation and TESS-band contrast. Gaia astrometry excludes bright companions only inside about 0.1 arcsec (TIC 67502817) and 0.3 arcsec (TIC 63562537).

citations.reason: Discovery of both candidates and the ephemerides that we test. Our independent tests find no false positive and support both as likely planets; we also prefer the second of its two period aliases for TIC 63562537.01.
